chunks: Muḥammad ibn Ḥassān narrated from Abī ʿImrān al-Armanī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Ḥakam, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who became bankrupt and owed a debt to some people, while some of them had pledged collateral and others did not. Then he died, and his wealth was not sufficient to cover the debt upon him.
He عليه السلام said: 'All that he left behind, including the pledged collateral and other property, is to be divided among the creditors according to their proportional shares.'

key_terms.أَرْبَابِ الدَّيْنِ: the creditors, those entitled to repayment

ai.seo_question: How are a deceased bankrupt debtor’s assets and pledged collateral divided among creditors in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning an insolvent debtor who dies while owing multiple creditors, some of whom possess collateral. The Imam عليه السلام rules that all the deceased’s remaining property, including the collateral, is distributed among the creditors proportionally according to their shares of the debt.
